A QUANTUM MURNAGHAN–NAKAYAMA RULE
FOR THE FLAG MANIFOLD
C. BENEDETTI, N. BERGERON, L. COLMENAREJO, F. SALIOLA, AND F. SOTTILE
Abstract. In this paper, we give a rule for the multiplication of a Schubert class by a
tautological class in the (small) quantum cohomology ring of the ﬂag manifold. As an inter-
mediate step, we establish a formula for the multiplication of a Schubert class by a quantum
Schur polynomial indexed by a hook partition. This entails a detailed analysis of chains and
intervals in the quantum Bruhat order. This

blocks.title: Grassmannian–Bruhat order
Minimal permutations
blocks.content:
[]{#minimal-permutations label="minimal-permutations"}

A permutation $\zeta$ is if ${\mathcal L}(\zeta) = \#\mathop{\mathrm{supp}}(\zeta) - s(\zeta)$, where ${\color{RoyalBlue}s(\zeta)}$ is the number of (nontrivial) cycles in the factorization of $\zeta$ into disjoint cycles. Minimality is a central concept in this paper. This terminology (introduced in [@BS-Bruhat]) arises from the inequality ${\mathcal L}(\zeta) \geq \#\mathop{\mathrm{supp}}(\zeta) - s(\zeta)$, so that a minimal permutation has the minimal possible rank given its cycle structure. blocks.title: A Murnaghan–Nakayama rule for quantum cohomology
blocks.content:
[]{#S:qCoh label="S:qCoh"}

The (small) quantum cohomology ring $qH^*{\mathbb F}\ell_n$ of the flag manifold is a deformation of the ordinary cohomology ring $H^*{\mathbb F}\ell_n$ whose product encodes the three-point Gromov--Witten invariants of ${\mathbb F}\ell_n$. We describe this ring and extend the main objects from Section [\[sec:classic-mn-rule\]](#sec:classic-mn-rule){reference-type="ref" reference="sec:classic-mn-rule"} to the quantum setting.

blocks.title: Left operators
blocks.content:
[]{#left-operators label="left-operators"}

We will prove the following quantum analog of the first part of Proposition [\[P:peaklessChains\]](#P:peaklessChains){reference-type="ref" reference="P:peaklessChains"}.

::: theorem
[]{#Th:nonZero label="Th:nonZero"} Let $u,w\in S_n$ and $q^\alpha w\in S_n[q]$ be such that $[u,q^\alpha w]^q_k$ is a minimal interval. Then there is a hook partition $\lambda$ with $|\lambda|=\ell(q^\alpha w)-\ell(u)$ such that $C^{q^\alpha w}_{u,v(\lambda,k)}$ is nonzero.
:::

blocks.title: Symmetries of the quantum k-Bruhat order
blocks.content:
[]{#sec:actions-on-left-operators label="sec:actions-on-left-operators"}

Operations that preserve the $k$-Bruhat order (its symmetries) played a role in many results in [@BS-Bruhat]. We identify three operations preserving the quantum $k$-Bruhat order, which are symmetries of that order. These induce three operations on the operators ${\mathbf v}_{ab}$ that preserve equivalence to ${\mathbf 0}$ and $(u,k)$-equivalence, and which are fundamental to our proof of Theorem [\[Th:nonZero\]](#Th:nonZero){reference-type="ref" reference="Th:nonZero"}. []{#ss:Paths label="ss:Paths"} We turn our attention to nonzero paths and simply call them paths from now on.
